$comment: Dev bench scenarios (docs/DEV_TOOLS.md; scripts/scenarios.ts describes the steps, scripts/bench.ts runs them). Each runs in a fresh local world: the player at the spawn, then the steps in order.

scenarios.name: lava-burn
scenarios.notes: Burning (VOLCANOES.md §6.3): an adventure-mode player on the starter's summit, the lake filled fast, the player put into the lava (`goto` the nearest dwell:lava): the red-orange screen edge and the sizzle.

scenarios.name: lava-glow
scenarios.notes: Lava's look by heat (VOLCANOES.md §6.5): every vent ×30 for 45 s, the summit lake by day and night, the face-B river running (hot), then the vents all but stopped for 40 s so the river cools by stop (warm, cooling, crusting).

scenarios.name: lava-lake
scenarios.notes: Lava's look (VOLCANOES.md §6.3): the starter world's summit lava lake, its vent's rate × 30 (the dev `lava` step) so it fills in seconds, by day and by night, the frame near it; then a dev vent by the sea for lava meeting water (obsidian, steam).

scenarios.name: memory-phone
scenarios.notes: A phone's memory (BUGS.md #70; run with --touch for the phone tier): an iPhone-sized page, memory() at the end of loading and 30 s later. A test world by --compare with a params config ({"worldgen": "test:starter"}). Keep the total well under 1 GB: iOS Safari reloads a tab over ~1-1.5 GB.

scenarios.name: idle-spawn
scenarios.notes: Standing at the spawn looking at the horizon once the LOD has loaded: the steady-state frame.

scenarios.name: fly-low-fast
scenarios.notes: Flying fast (level 6, 64 m/s) about 15 m over the terrain (owner, 2026-10-14: the hitch seen when flying low): full-detail chunks streaming in as fast as the player moves. Heading +X (yaw 90) from the seed-7 spawn: a clear 1.7 km (flying is stopped by any ledge it hits: low enough to stream full-detail chunks, high enough not to snag).

scenarios.name: fly-low-faster
scenarios.notes: Flying fast (level 8, 128 m/s) about 15 m over the terrain (owner, 2026-10-14: the hitch seen when flying low): full-detail chunks streaming in as fast as the player moves. Heading +X (yaw 90) from the seed-7 spawn: a clear 1.7 km (flying is stopped by any ledge it hits: low enough to stream full-detail chunks, high enough not to snag).

scenarios.name: jump-onto-block
scenarios.notes: Places a block in front of the spawn, walks into it and jumps with forward held (owner, 2026-10-14: the jump usually failed to clear one block): the player should land on top (grounded 1 m up), then walk off its far side.

scenarios.name: water-views
scenarios.notes: The sea seen four ways (Phase 26 W1b, the water shader): goes to the world map's nearest deep sea from the seed-7 spawn (`goto` with scope world: at least 2 m deep and 1000 cells wide, the player moved there), then views it from 2 m up across the sea, its back to the nearest beach, at a low angle; toward the beach from 5 m up; with the eye just under the surface; and from 1 km up. Records the frame over the sea. Finding no such sea fails the run.

scenarios.name: water-shore
scenarios.notes: The shore in the water's depth views (Phase 26 W3): goes to the world map's nearest deep sea from the seed-7 spawn as water-views does, then to the beach nearest it (`goto land`: the nearest dry ground; the player moved there) and shoots the beach edge at a low angle toward the water, straight down into the shallows by the beach, the deep-to-shallow gradient from 20 m up over the sea toward the beach, under the surface in the shallows (the floor and its caustics, along it, up toward the surface) and the far water from 1 km. Finding no sea or beach fails the run.

scenarios.name: water-reflections
scenarios.notes: The water's reflections (Phase 26 W5a: land by screen-space reflection, clouds along the reflected ray) on Medium: goes to the world map's nearest deep sea from the seed-7 spawn as water-views does, then from 1.5 m over the water shoots the nearest beach and the land behind it at a low angle (recorded: the cost), turned and steeper; then, the player moved to the beach, from the water nearest it at several pitches and from the side (the screen-edge fades); the clouds in the sea; then the beach at dusk and at night and the low sun over the water. Finding no sea or beach fails the run.

scenarios.name: water-river
scenarios.notes: A river's flow visuals (docs/WATER_SURFACE_GRID.md §2c): goes to the world map's nearest river from the seed-7 spawn and finds water running at least 0.1 m/s there, then views it from 2 m up downstream and upstream, across it from 6 m up (steeply: a narrow river's banks rise close), and from 12 m up looking down on it. Records the frame looking downstream. Finding no running river fails the run.

scenarios.name: water-flood
scenarios.notes: A flood for the water's re-mesh cost (proposals/WATER_GPU_SURFACE.md C6a): goes to the seed-7 spawn's nearest running river as water-river does, then clears a 29 × 29 m box from 1 m to 5 m under the feet (the river's bed and both banks under its level), so the river pours in from up- and downstream and fills the pit, viewed from 12 m up looking down. Records the 12 s of the fill; compare with the `heightfield` configuration (the near water from the GPU heightfield: level-only changes rewrite tiles instead of re-meshing).

scenarios.name: jump-in-place
scenarios.notes: Jumps on flat ground at the spawn: the controller trace shows the jump's peak.

scenarios.name: look-horizon
scenarios.notes: From the player's eyes at the spawn, looking along the ground 3° below the horizon (heading +X): a grazing view over near and far terrain.

scenarios.name: look-down
scenarios.notes: From the player's eyes at the spawn, looking 80° down at the ground: near terrain only.

scenarios.name: edit-burst
scenarios.notes: Places and breaks a block in front of the spawn 150 times each (300 edits, about one per 0.12 s, just over the edit interval): the cost of remeshing and uploading edited chunks.

scenarios.name: shadows-pines
scenarios.notes: Sun shadows in a pine grove (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §10): mid-morning, rises a little over the spawn and looks across the groves up the hill (recorded: the cost of the maps with many casters), then shoots the pines' shadows on High, Low and Off.

scenarios.name: shadows-still
scenarios.notes: Shadow flicker with a still camera (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §10): hovers over the spawn looking across the pine groves, then shoots bursts of frames back to back at noon and at dusk (and at noon looking down at the ground under you, the nearest cascade's), with the time of day held and with it running at the world clock's rate (the light moving every frame, as in play), on High, Low and Off. Read each burst's flicker (the share of pixels that change from frame to frame) against the Off burst's (the clouds, water and plants' own motion).

scenarios.name: lod-zfight
scenarios.notes: The LOD's z-fighting (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.6, "Known bug class"; owner 2026-10-21: dirt showing through the grass from high up, changing as the camera moves): the camera placed 160–300 m over the seed-7 spawn's hills at three pitches with the phone's detail (128 m full detail, 8 px), drifting 2 mm and 0.002° a frame through a 16-frame burst. Fails when over 0.004 % of the pixels flip hue between frames (grass to dirt): 0.005–0.013 % before the fix (top skirts on the section plane in the top row's dirt colour), 0.000–0.002 % after.

scenarios.name: lod-zfight-b
scenarios.notes: lod-zfight on face B (its noon is face A's midnight): the same heights over face B's spawn, along its up.

scenarios.name: climb-fast
scenarios.notes: Flies straight up at level 8 (about 176 m/s) for 4 s from the settled spawn, then hovers 3 s: the chunks above arrive over the ones below, and the ones below are dropped in batches (the flood light's relights: 0.22.9 had 1.2-1.6 s long tasks here, 0.22.8 none over 50 ms). Read the long tasks and the frame interval's max.

scenarios.name: fly-high
scenarios.notes: Flies up about 540 m (level 8 for 3 s), looks out and down 20° and flies +X for 10 s: far terrain, the LOD's distant levels streaming.

scenarios.name: thermal-10min
scenarios.notes: Phone-oriented: ten minutes of flight 60 m up at level 4 (32 m/s) round a 660 m square, for thermal throttling: the last minute's frame intervals against the first's. Run it on a phone (or with the device's own heat in mind); it takes over ten minutes.

scenarios.name: day-night
scenarios.notes: The day/night cycle (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md): from 2 s of flight above the seed-7 spawn, each time of day looking toward the sun (or the moon by night) and away from it, then the moon at three phases.

scenarios.name: day-timelapse
scenarios.notes: A whole day in 48 frames looking along the sun's path toward sunset (yaw -150), from above the spawn.

scenarios.name: day-night-cost
scenarios.notes: The day/night cycle's GPU cost (run with --unthrottled; clouds off, so the sky is the cycle alone): the spawn view at noon and at midnight (the stars drawn), and looking up into the sky at both.

scenarios.name: sprint-straight
scenarios.notes: Sprints (Shift + W) along +X from the seed-7 spawn (Phase 29 motion effects): the FOV widens by the sprint boost and faint wind streaks show at the screen's edges; a shot standing, mid-sprint, then standing again.

scenarios.name: fly-fast-turn
scenarios.notes: Flies fast (level 8 with Run: the terrain band's 400 m/s cap) from the seed-7 spawn, then turns and dives (Phase 29 motion effects): the strong flight streaks, and the vanishing point following the direction of travel as the view turns away from it.

scenarios.name: clouds-high
scenarios.notes: The sky's clouds on High (docs/CLOUDS.md): shots looking up, at the horizon and toward the sun, then 5 s recorded looking 25° up (mostly sky). Run with --unthrottled to compare gpu.composite between clouds-high, clouds-low and clouds-off.

scenarios.name: clouds-low
scenarios.notes: clouds-high on Low (fewer octaves, no self-shadow).

scenarios.name: clouds-off
scenarios.notes: clouds-high with the clouds off: the baseline for their GPU cost.

scenarios.name: clouds-night
scenarios.notes: The clouds by moonlight (midnight).

scenarios.name: clouds-dusk
scenarios.notes: The clouds with a low sun (golden hour, the sun about 5° up toward yaw −152), toward it and away.

scenarios.name: clouds-fly
scenarios.notes: Flying fast (level 10, 256 m/s) climbing toward the cloud deck: the clouds move past with parallax and drift; shots every few seconds, the last looking up from near the deck as the clouds fade.

scenarios.name: clouds-altitude
scenarios.notes: The camera placed 1000 m, 1500 m and 1700 m up (the deck is at 1800 m): the clouds come nearer and larger, then fade out as the eye reaches the deck.

scenarios.name: day-night-face-b
scenarios.notes: The day/night cycle on face B (DAY_NIGHT.md §3): a camera 50 m over face B's ground at the origin (y = −452: seed 7's face B stands 402 m high there; the old −4,150, from before Phase 16's midplane at 0, put the camera inside the rock, the "stray dark slabs", BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §11); face A's noon is face B's midnight (the moon overhead), face A's sunset is face B's sunrise.

scenarios.name: clouds-above
scenarios.notes: The cloud deck (1.8 km up) seen from above (CLOUDS.md §7): the camera 3.5 km up looking down at 40°, then 15 km up (a cloud sea to the deck's horizon), then 5 s recorded 3.5 km up looking down (the deck over the terrain: compare gpu.composite with clouds-off).

scenarios.name: clouds-above-off
scenarios.notes: clouds-above's recorded view with the clouds off: the baseline for the deck's cost from above.

scenarios.name: clouds-far-above
scenarios.notes: The cloud deck from 3–40 km up over seed 7, by day and by night (owner, 2026-10-21: from high up the clouds showed in a circle round the player and past the world's edge, not over the far sea; CLOUDS.md §7): the deck must cover the whole flat world below its altitude.

scenarios.name: clouds-far-above-b
scenarios.notes: clouds-far-above on face B (its noon is face A's midnight): the camera 15 and 40 km out along face B's up.

scenarios.name: clouds-through
scenarios.notes: Rising through the deck (1.8 km): the camera at 1.3, 1.65, 1.8, 1.95 and 2.3 km looking 10° down: the deck fades out below it, the in-cloud fog where a cloud is, then the deck's top below. No pop between the shots. At the deck's height also at x = 1.5, 3, 4.5 and 6 km, so some shots are inside a cloud (the in-cloud fog).

scenarios.name: clouds-level
scenarios.notes: At the deck's height (1.8 km) looking at the horizon, and 100 m above and below it.

scenarios.name: clouds-above-night
scenarios.notes: The deck from above by moonlight (midnight), 3.5 km up looking down at 30°.

scenarios.name: clouds-above-fast
scenarios.notes: The deck from above at speed (owner's report, 2026-10-20: the clouds showed only inside a circle). Climbs at level 10 (256 m/s) above the deck (1.8 km), then flies fast with Run looking 40° and 80° down: the wind's edge blur over the deck where it is in front of the terrain. The clouds must reach the view's edges, as they do flying slowly.

scenarios.name: walk-over-a-placed-block
scenarios.notes: Places a block in front of the spawn and walks over it without jumping (Phase 18, ADAPTIVE_BLOCKS.md): natural ground shapes itself, so the placed block is a half pyramid (45° faces: a slide, owner 2026-10-15) and the ground under and around it ramps up at 27° — the controller trace shows what the player does on it (no jump, no launch).

scenarios.name: slide-off-a-steep-block
scenarios.notes: Slides on 45° ground (PLAYER_CONTROLLER.md §6.8, owner 2026-10-15): places a block in front of the spawn (natural ground shapes it into a half pyramid with 45° faces), walks up the 27° ground around it into its 45° face (walking up it fails: the player slides back, braking), steers right along the face mid-slide with forward still held, then lets go and slides off. The controller trace (records.slide.ticks) shows the Sliding state, the speeds and the steer; the sounds (window.__dwell.sounds) the slide's loop and stop.

scenarios.name: sprint-slide
scenarios.notes: The sprint slide (PLAYER_CONTROLLER.md §6.9, owner 2026-10-19): sprints (Shift+W), presses crouch (C) to slide on in the crouch capsule, steers right (D) mid-slide, jumps out (Space) keeping the momentum; then, crouch let go, sprints and slides again after the cooldown and rides it out to the crouch speed. Screenshots through the slide (the lower eye, the FOV widening); the controller trace (records.slide.ticks) shows the Sliding state, the crouch flag, the speed falling with friction and the jump; the sounds the crouch and the slide's scrape.

scenarios.name: slopes-near-far
scenarios.notes: Natural slopes from the player's eyes, looking down at the ground nearby and out to the horizon (Phase 18): screenshots of the adaptive shapes near (chunks) and far (the LOD's sloped tops), and the steady frame there.

scenarios.name: spyglass-far
scenarios.notes: The spyglass (docs/SPYGLASS.md): flies about 180 m up over the seed-7 spawn and looks out over the distant terrain 6° down (heading +X), then shoots it unzoomed, zoomed to each step once the LOD has refined inside the narrow view, and unzoomed again.

scenarios.name: step-up-angles
scenarios.notes: The step-up from many angles (PLAYER_CONTROLLER.md §4) on the generated ground: walks, then runs, out and back at 24 headings (every 15°) from the spawn, 1.2 s each way. The controller traces (records 'walk' and 'run') show each step-up (a grounded feet rise) and any hang-up (forward input held, grounded, the speed near zero).

scenarios.name: faces-a
scenarios.notes: Face parity's look (BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §11): other players' bodies, your arms, the block outline, the sky and clouds and the spyglass on face A; `faces-b` is the same on face B, to compare shot for shot.

scenarios.name: faces-b
scenarios.notes: `faces-a` on face B (the player and the puppets on face B's spawn).

scenarios.name: tunnel-a
scenarios.notes: A hill built in front of the spawn (stone, 32 m long, 15 m tall) with a 3 m wide, 2 m tall tunnel 20 m into it; walked into at noon and at midnight. Owner's bug (2026-10-21, "lit up like day"; DAY_NIGHT.md §11): the tunnel goes dark inside, your hand with it.

scenarios.name: tunnel-b
scenarios.notes: tunnel-a on face B (its noon is face A midnight: time 0 is noon here, 0.5 midnight). Owner's bug (2026-10-21, "lit up like day"; DAY_NIGHT.md §11): the tunnel goes dark inside, your hand with it.

scenarios.name: lod-shadows-dusk
scenarios.notes: The distant terrain's shadows (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §12): a camera 520 m up over the seed-7 hills with a low sun (time 0.81, then 0.795), looking away from the sun and across it, past the shadow cascades; records 5 s of the first view (with --compare and lod-shadows-off: the third layer's cost).

scenarios.name: lod-shadows-dusk-b
scenarios.notes: lod-shadows-dusk on face B: the camera 520 m under the midplane over face B's hills, its low sun at face A's time 0.855, then 0.87 (just after face A's sunset, face B's sunrise), four headings.

scenarios.name: torch-cave-a
scenarios.notes: A hill with a tunnel into a room (as tunnel-a), at midnight: walked into the dark, then holding the torch (picked into slot 6) and placing it on the floor (docs/LIGHTS.md). Shots: dark-no-torch, held-torch, held-torch-wall, placed-torch, placed-torch-room.

scenarios.name: torch-cave-b
scenarios.notes: A hill with a tunnel into a room (as tunnel-a), at midnight: walked into the dark, then holding the torch (picked into slot 6) and placing it on the floor (docs/LIGHTS.md). Shots: dark-no-torch, held-torch, held-torch-wall, placed-torch, placed-torch-room. On face B (its midnight is time 0.5).

scenarios.name: torch-night-puppets
scenarios.notes: Midnight in the open (docs/LIGHTS.md): 8 stand-in players holding the hotbar's block, first the torch (slot 9: 8 held lights and yours, the light budget) then stone (no lights). Records torches and no-torches for the cost of the dynamic lights.

scenarios.name: torch-scale-a
scenarios.notes: The 1 m torch (two ½ m cells, docs/LIGHTS.md) placed on the ground ahead at noon, a stand-in player beside it for scale, then at midnight; and the held torch's flame (self-lit) by day and at night.

scenarios.name: torch-shadows-a
scenarios.notes: Torch shadows (docs/LIGHTS.md §4): the tunnel and room of torch-cave-a at midnight with a stone pillar in the room; a torch placed before it (its shadow on the floor and wall behind), then the torch held as well. Records placed and held-and-placed for the maps' cost; run with --configs torch-shadows-off,torch-shadows-high.

scenarios.name: torch-shadows-b
scenarios.notes: Torch shadows (docs/LIGHTS.md §4): the tunnel and room of torch-cave-a at midnight with a stone pillar in the room; a torch placed before it (its shadow on the floor and wall behind), then the torch held as well. Records placed and held-and-placed for the maps' cost; run with --configs torch-shadows-off,torch-shadows-high. On face B (its midnight is time 0.5).

scenarios.name: join-behind
scenarios.notes: The join's timeline (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3, §6.6): looks +X the moment the game starts and shoots ahead and behind (−X), then waits until the full detail behind the camera has loaded (until nearBehind: within the full-detail distance), then nothing behind is still loading (until behind: every LOD section and chunk out of view), then ahead, then settles and shoots behind again. Formerly the out-of-view LOD ranked as if its cells were 8 times smaller, so the terrain behind loaded only after the whole view ahead (or once the player turned round). Run with --compare --configs raster,loading-off for the loading screen's cost.

scenarios.name: respawn-far
scenarios.notes: The respawn's timeline (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3, owner 2026-10-21: "We could preload terrain at spawn once you die too?"): flies about 700 m east of the seed-7 spawn (level 6, as fly-low-fast), waits there while the view loads (the spawn's chunks leave), dies, and times respawn → playing behind the loading screen (the report's respawns). With the respawn preload the server streams the spawn's ring and the client meshes it and readies its LOD during the five-second death screen. Run with --compare --configs raster,respawn-preload-off for the preload's effect.

scenarios.name: portal-a
scenarios.notes: A portal between the faces (BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §12, shared/worldgen/midplane.json): seed 7's nearest the centre (axis column -4872, 20185), the player on face A's rim over its ladder (?spawn=portal). Shots: the opening from above, the shaft looked down from over its axis, the midplane from inside the shaft, then the climb down the ladder looking down and holding forward: just above the midplane, across it (the look continued: up face B's ladder), and at face B's opening.

scenarios.name: portal-b
scenarios.notes: The same portal's face B opening (seed 7; ?spawn=portal-b): the player on face B's rim over the ladder. Shots: the opening from above (face B's up), the shaft looked down from over its axis.

scenarios.name: portal-motes
scenarios.notes: The glowing motes in a portal's shaft round the midplane (BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §12.1, shared/look/motes.json), seed 7's nearest portal (?spawn=portal): from above the midplane, at it (twice, 0.7 s apart: they swirl and pulse), and climbing down the ladder into them. Records motes.drawn.

scenarios.name: felling
scenarios.notes: Felling (docs/FELLING.md): on the flat world, a log trunk with a leaf crown (picked into slot 6) built before the player, its trunk broken near the base: it tips away, falls and settles as logs lying on the ground. Shots: tree, fall-a, fall-b, fall-c, settled.

scenarios.name: axe
scenarios.notes: The stone axe as weighty melee (ADR 0067, 0.50.38): on the flat world a log trunk 1.5 m ahead with a leaf crown; the axe (picked into slot 6) held in both grips, a free swing at the sky, a bounce off the ground, notching swings with shots of the impact, the deep notch, the lean, the leaves, and the fall.

scenarios.name: damage-dents
scenarios.notes: Block damage's dents (docs/BLOCK_DAMAGE.md §6): on the flat world, a dirt patch and a stone block before the player; the shovel hits the dirt twice (dirt-2) and twice more (dirt-4), the stone pickaxe hits the stone three times (stone-3).

scenarios.name: dirt-relief
scenarios.notes: Block damage's carved dents (docs/BLOCK_DAMAGE.md §6.1): damage-dents' dirt patch dug 2 and 4 times, each shot from standing height and close up, by day (0.42) and at a low sun (0.27).
